findings.description: External call to ammAdapter.swap(vault, underlyingToken, sharesToSell, minOut) at line 328 happens before state updates clientBalances[token][balanceHolder] -= amount (line 335) and totalDeposited[token] -= amount (line 336). Function is protected by nonReentrant on the public entry-points (withdraw / withdrawAsOwner via AYieldStrategy), but the principal-decrement-after-call pattern is flagged for review since the ammAdapter is owner-configured.

External call to ammAdapter.swap(vault, underlyingToken, sharesToSell, minOut) at line 390 happens before clientBalances[token][client] = 0 (line 393) and totalDeposited[token] -= clientStoredBalance (line 394). _totalWithdraw is reached from the two-phase emergency flow, which is owner-gated but also worth reviewing for re-entrant ammAdapter behavior.

External call to ammAdapter.swap before clientBalances[token][recipient] += amount and totalDeposited[token] += amount. Same pattern as withdraw; classified benign by Slither (writes are increments). Worth verifying that no read-before-update logic depends on these mappings on re-entry.

Strict equality check `totalShares == 0 || totalDeposited[token] == 0` is used to early-return in _totalWithdraw. If, in the two-phase emergency flow, vault balance has drifted to zero through previous withdrawals while clientBalances are non-zero, the strict equality silently returns, leaving the client's tracked balance non-zero on the books even though no underlying was delivered. Worth confirming the state machine guarantees this is recoverable.

Local variable `address lastToken` declared without initializer, then populated by walking `path` looking for the highest non-zero entry. Default value `address(0)` would fail the `lastToken == tokenOut` check (since tokenOut is required non-zero on line 70), so functionally safe today. Flagged because the loop logic depends on path containing at least one non-zero entry past index 0, which is enforced indirectly by `path[0] == tokenIn` (line 71). Cosmetic, but consider initializing for clarity.

Local variable `uint256 totalSetAside` is declared without an initializer at line 510, accumulated inside the loop, and returned (or used to compute `toRecipient`). Default uint256 zero is the intended start value; this is safe but the explicit `= 0` would be cleaner. Cosmetic only.

External call `vault.convertToShares(surplus)` executed once per client inside the loop in _accrueSurplusShares (reached from skimSurplus). For an ERC4626 vault this is a low-gas view call, but griefing/DoS scales linearly in the number of authorized clients. If the authorized-client set is owner-curated and small, impact is bounded; otherwise worth tracking gas.
